key_points: Identifies the network portion of an IP address
Identifies the host portion of an IP address
Q1.correct: Covers both network and host identification.
Q1.partial: Covers only one of the two portions, or gives a vague partial answer.
Q1.incorrect: Contradicts the reference, negates the purpose, or is irrelevant.

key_points: Resolves human-readable domain names
Maps names to numerical IP addresses
Q2.correct: Explains resolving names to IP addresses.
Q2.partial: Mentions only one aspect (names or IPs).
Q2.incorrect: Confuses DNS with hosting, email, or negates its function.

key_points: Acknowledgements confirm receipt of data segments
Retransmissions recover lost or unacknowledged packets
Q3.correct: Covers both ACKs confirming receipt and retransmissions recovering lost data.
Q3.partial: Covers only acknowledgements or only retransmissions.
Q3.incorrect: Claims TCP never resends data, confuses with UDP, or negates either mechanism.

key_points: Forwards packets between different networks at Layer 3
Uses routing table to select the optimal next hop
Q4.correct: Explains inter-network forwarding using routing tables.
Q4.partial: Mentions forwarding or routing table but not both.
Q4.incorrect: Confuses router with switch, states routers don't forward packets, or is irrelevant.

key_points: Logically groups switch ports or devices
Creates distinct Layer 2 broadcast domains
Q5.correct: Explains logical grouping AND separate broadcast domains.
Q5.partial: Mentions only grouping or only broadcast domain isolation.
Q5.incorrect: Confuses VLAN with VPN tunnel, physical wiring, or negates the grouping.

key_points: IP address is logical Layer 3 used for routing
MAC address is physical Layer 2 for local frame delivery
Q6.correct: Contrasts logical routing role of IP with physical local-delivery role of MAC.
Q6.partial: Correctly describes only IP or only MAC.
Q6.incorrect: Swaps the definitions, calls them identical, or negates both.

key_points: Acts as the router interface/exit point for the local subnet
Forwards packets to remote or external networks
Q7.correct: Explains exit point role and forwarding to remote networks.
Q7.partial: Mentions router without explaining remote forwarding or exit point role.
Q7.incorrect: Confuses gateway with DNS/DHCP or states it doesn't forward external traffic.

key_points: HTTP transmits unencrypted plain text
HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption for security and integrity
Q8.correct: Explains plain-text HTTP vs SSL/TLS-encrypted HTTPS.
Q8.partial: Mentions only that HTTPS is secure without explaining plain text vs encryption.
Q8.incorrect: Claims HTTP is encrypted or negates HTTPS encryption.

key_points: Process has its own independent memory address space
Thread shares memory within the same process
Q9.correct: Explains separate address space of processes vs shared memory of threads.
Q9.partial: Mentions only process isolation or only thread sharing.
Q9.incorrect: Reverses memory ownership or claims threads have separate address spaces.

key_points: Uses secondary disk storage as an extension of physical RAM
Enables programs larger than physical memory and provides isolation
Q10.correct: Covers disk extension of RAM and enabling large programs or isolation.
Q10.partial: Mentions only disk extension or only large program execution.
Q10.incorrect: Confuses virtual memory with cloud storage, registers, or negates disk usage.

key_points: Two or more processes are permanently blocked
Circular wait: each holds a resource the other needs
Q11.correct: Explains permanent blocking AND circular resource waiting.
Q11.partial: Mentions blocked processes without circular wait, or waiting without permanent block.
Q11.incorrect: Claims deadlock is a CPU crash, code loop, or negates blocking.

key_points: Primary key uniquely identifies records and cannot be null
Foreign key references a primary key in another table
Q12.correct: Covers uniqueness/non-null of PK and referential role of FK.
Q12.partial: Defines only PK or only FK.
Q12.incorrect: Swaps definitions or claims FK must be unique in its own table.

key_points: All-or-nothing: all operations succeed or none do
Rolls back all changes on any failure
Q13.correct: Covers all-or-nothing execution and rollback on failure.
Q13.partial: Mentions only one aspect (all-or-nothing or rollback).
Q13.incorrect: Confuses with isolation/speed, or negates rollback behaviour.

key_points: Accelerates query retrieval speed
Avoids full table scans using an organised data structure
Q14.correct: Covers speed improvement and avoiding full scans.
Q14.partial: Mentions only speed or only avoiding scans.
Q14.incorrect: Claims indexes compress data or prevent duplicates; negates speed benefit.

key_points: Minimises data redundancy
Eliminates insertion, update, and deletion anomalies
Q15.correct: Covers reducing redundancy AND eliminating anomalies.
Q15.partial: Mentions only one of the two goals.
Q15.incorrect: Confuses normalisation with encryption, hashing, or negates redundancy reduction.

key_points: Client sends SYN; server responds with SYN-ACK
Client sends final ACK establishing full-duplex connection
Q16.correct: Describes the full SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK exchange.
Q16.partial: Mentions three steps but omits naming the control flags or the purpose.
Q16.incorrect: Claims TCP is connectionless, confuses with TLS handshake, or negates the steps.

key_points: Resolves known IP address to physical MAC address
Operates on the local network segment for frame delivery
Q17.correct: Explains IP-to-MAC resolution on the local link.
Q17.partial: Mentions address resolution without specifying IP-to-MAC or local scope.
Q17.incorrect: Reverses direction (MAC to IP) or claims ARP routes globally.

key_points: TCP is connection-oriented and guarantees reliable in-order delivery
UDP is connectionless and low-latency without delivery guarantees
Q18.correct: Contrasts TCP reliability/ordering with UDP connectionless/low-latency nature.
Q18.partial: Correctly describes only TCP or only UDP.
Q18.incorrect: Claims UDP is more reliable than TCP, or that both use handshakes.

key_points: Automatically assigns dynamic IP addresses to clients
Also provides subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS parameters
Q19.correct: Covers automatic IP assignment AND providing network config parameters.
Q19.partial: Mentions only IP assignment without network config parameters.
Q19.incorrect: Confuses DHCP with DNS, claims DHCP is an encryption tool.

key_points: Preemptive scheduling can interrupt a running process
Non-preemptive scheduling lets a process keep the CPU until it yields or finishes
Q20.correct: Correctly contrasts preemptive interruption with non-preemptive voluntary release.
Q20.partial: Correctly describes only one of the two scheduling types.
Q20.incorrect: Reverses the definitions or confuses scheduling with memory paging.

key_points: Divides memory into fixed-size pages and frames
Non-contiguous allocation eliminates external fragmentation
Q21.correct: Covers fixed-size pages/frames AND non-contiguous allocation eliminating external fragmentation.
Q21.partial: Mentions pages and frames without explaining the fragmentation elimination, or vice versa.
Q21.incorrect: Claims paging causes external fragmentation, or confuses with disk defragmentation.

key_points: Mutex has ownership: only the locking thread can unlock
Binary semaphore has no ownership and can be signalled by any thread
Q22.correct: Correctly explains mutex ownership vs semaphore's absence of ownership.
Q22.partial: States both are synchronisation primitives without explaining ownership difference.
Q22.incorrect: Claims any thread can unlock a mutex, or swaps the ownership rules.

key_points: Clustered index physically orders and stores data rows (one per table)
Non-clustered index is a separate pointer structure referencing data rows
Q23.correct: Correctly contrasts physical storage ordering (clustered) with separate pointer structure (non-clustered).
Q23.partial: Correctly defines only clustered or only non-clustered index.
Q23.incorrect: Claims a table can have many clustered indexes, or swaps the definitions.

key_points: Concurrent transactions execute independently without interference
Prevents dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads
Q24.correct: Covers independent execution AND prevention of concurrency anomalies.
Q24.partial: Mentions independence without naming the anomalies prevented, or vice versa.
Q24.incorrect: Confuses isolation with durability or claims isolation eliminates the need for locking.

key_points: WHERE filters rows before any grouping or aggregation
HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY is applied
Q25.correct: Correctly contrasts row-level filtering before grouping (WHERE) with group-level filtering after aggregation (HAVING).
Q25.partial: Correctly describes only WHERE or only HAVING.
Q25.incorrect: Claims WHERE can filter aggregates or swaps the clause purposes.
